result.summary:
Wrote /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C06/partura/s803/r3/lit.md, answering the 4 literature questions (L1-L4) at the end of r3/analysis.md, using only WebSearch results from pre-2023-08-08 sources (no reads of other seeds, C01-C05, guidance/C0*, runs/lab/notes/etc., or any post-2023-08-08 numbers, per rules.md).

Per topic, wrote concrete treatments translatable into the team's operator language, each tagged with a citation:
- L1 (core ①, ts_reg_fvalue as a goodness-of-fit characteristic): Morck-Yeung-Yu / Roll R²-as-synchronicity literature, plus Gassen-Skaife-Veenman (2020) showing this R² is mechanically biased downward by illiquidity -- directly backs the team's planned periphery step 1 (bucket by trading-density decile before trusting the core). Also Scholes-Williams (1977) nonsynchronous-trading bias precedent, and Admati-Pfleiderer (1988) / Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (2010) on why intraday trading-concentration shape correlates with liquidity rather than necessarily carrying new information.
- L2 (unnormalized higher realized moments vs volatility; ListAge; China low-vol long leg): Amaya et al. (2015 JFE) and Neuberger (2012 RFS) give the standard normalization (divide by RV^1.5), which is literally the R2-6 "dimensionless" variant's denominator -- strong formal match, though no paper was found stating outright that the unnormalized version "is" volatility level (flagged as not found). Liu-Stambaugh-Yuan (2019 JFE) "Size and Value in China" gives the China-specific precedent for screening out small/shell stocks rather than mining them, bearing on ListAge. Robeco (2021) industry report and a peer-reviewed 2021 Discrete Dynamics paper (title/author not fully confirmed, flagged) support a long-only low-vol effect in China pre-cutoff; one Tianjin University quantile-regression paper is noted as contested evidence.
- L3 (N-甲, overnight/intraday split): Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019 JFE / 2015 LSE working paper) is the originating "tug of war" methodology match. Qiao & Dam (2020 JFM) ties China's negative overnight return to the T+1 rule (a risk the team's plan hadn't flagged: overnight level correlates with vol control even without limit-hits). An-Huang-Li (2022) gives an asymmetric/conditional construction (condition on prior day's intraday sign) not yet in the plan. Zhou & Liu (2022, Frontiers in Energy Research) shows the sign can flip by sector in China. Added a new, previously unflagged risk: Shanghai's 2018-08-20 closing-call-auction introduction is a mid-sample structural break affecting day_last(Close) measurement that the overnight leg depends on.
- L4 (trading density as independent feature; sample-screening manufacturing factors): Lesmond-Ogden-Trzcinka (1999) and Bekaert-Harvey-Lundblad (2007) are direct precedents for zero-return-proportion as a liquidity signal outperforming turnover -- backs R1-2. Jones-Kaul-Lipson (1994) shows trade count (not dollar volume) drives the volume-volatility link, backing day_pos_ratio's conceptual basis. For the screening-bias half: Hou-Xue-Zhang (2020) "Replicating Anomalies" and Lesmond-Schill-Zhou (2004) are the closest (but not identical) precedents for "universe/screen construction can manufacture or erase an apparent factor" -- explicitly flagged as structurally analogous to, but not a direct statement of, the team's own engineering finding about pow_2_5's implicit NaN-based sample deletion (no literature found addressing that specific implicit-NaN mechanism).

Each topic's reference list gives title/authors/year-month/venue/link/verified(true|false) per rules; items I could not independently confirm (author full names, exact month, or a paper's full title from secondary citations only) are marked verified:false with the specific gap stated, never fabricated. Closed with a one-paragraph honesty note to the PI on which of the four topics have strong vs. only structurally-analogous literature backing.
